name: contributions
description: A member's claim for creation, and the moderation trail that decides it. A confirmed contribution produces a transaction.

columns.name: contribution_date
columns.description: The period the work was done in — what the creation is claimed for, not when it was submitted.

columns.name: contribution_link_id
columns.description: Set when the contribution came from a contribution link rather than being written by hand.

columns.name: transaction_id
columns.description: The CREATION row this produced. Null until confirmed.

columns.name: resubmission_at
columns.description: A moderator asked for changes and set a date to look again.

columns.name: creation_groups_set_at
columns.description: When the creation group was last set through the group field. NULL is the only case in which a legacy inline '#tag' in the memo still counts — once this carries a timestamp, hashtags in the text are free text.

notes: Unlike transactions this table is mutable: status moves PENDING -> IN_PROGRESS -> CONFIRMED or DENIED, and a moderator may ask for resubmission. It is therefore not a cursor table — a session caching contributions needs a version or generation, not a highest-id watermark. See Architecture.md, Consistency model.

Five separate actor columns (moderator_id, confirmed_by, denied_by, updated_by, deleted_by) with matching timestamps. Only one path may be taken: confirmed and denied are mutually exclusive, and both implementations must reject a row that carries both.
The transaction is created on confirmation, so transaction_id null with status CONFIRMED is an inconsistency, not a state.
Legacy declares deleted_by with TypeORM's @DeleteDateColumn although it holds a user id, not a date. Carried here as uint64, which is what the column actually is.
Timestamps are UTC milliseconds; see types/Timestamp.json. Legacy uses datetime without precision(3) on this table — second precision.
